title: The Billable Hour is Dead; Long Live the Billable Hour — Kevin Madura + Mo Bhasin, Alix Partners
talk_summary: Alix Partners describes an internal GenAI platform built around structured-output classification, enterprise RAG with API tool calls, and schema-based document extraction with logprob confidence. The practical lessons are to harden individual steps before chaining agents, wrap LLM outputs in validation, and use confidence signals for human review.

takeaways.technique: Logprob confidence gating for structured findings
takeaways.what_they_do: They align token logprobs with structured-output field values and use the geometric mean as a rough confidence score, highlighting low-confidence outputs for human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use the log probs that's returned from the OpenAI API and we align that with the output schema from structured outputs

takeaways.technique: Structured-output taxonomy classification with tool lookup
takeaways.what_they_do: They classify entities into a fixed taxonomy using structured outputs, and when the model lacks knowledge they tool-call a web/API lookup to append context before categorizing at volume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: enter tool call. You can run a web query to append information to each of these pieces of uh to each of these companies and then categorize enormous volumes.
takeaways.numbers: 95% accuracy across 10,000 vendors; minutes vs days; order of magnitude less cost

takeaways.technique: Teach the LLM an API spec instead of bespoke integrations
takeaways.what_they_do: They embed an API specification and teach the LLM to call that API, exposing siloed data sources through tool calls rather than manual UI/email workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we took the API spec, embedded it, and taught the LLM how to call an API

takeaways.technique: Harden single steps before chaining agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They build and validate individual classification/extraction steps to high robustness before daisy-chaining them into agentic workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: builds that individual step to a high level of robustness and accuracy

takeaways.technique: Stepwise retrieval instead of whole-corpus reasoning
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that a prompt like “reason across all documents” is not how RAG works and build retrieval solutions step by step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you say reason across all documents, that's just not how Rag works. So we have to build those solutions step by step

takeaways.technique: Schema plus validation scaffolding around LLM extraction
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine a document, an output schema, an LLM, and validation/scaffolding to ensure extracted values are usable and trustworthy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: combining a document with a schema with an LLM with some validation and scaffolding around it
